short: Differentiable-synthesizer decoding (M06) and autoencoder guidance (M02) are standard: the group posted both in 2021. New here: 48-participant scale; naturalness and generalization untested.
position: The paper [@chen2024neural] changes the intermediate representation (M06), 18 acoustic parameters rendered by a differentiable synthesizer, and the training-only supervision (M02), targets from a per-participant speech autoencoder. Both are standard for this paper: the group's 2021 preprint already had the pipeline, with causal and anticausal decoders, on five participants [@wang2023distributed], although none of 63 prior intracranial-synthesis ledger studies names a differentiable synthesizer (Appendix). What it adds is scale: 48 participants, three decoders, both hemispheres and a held-out-word test (5 of 202 prior studies, Appendix). The claim of natural speech in the speaker's voice is untested: the waveform comes from Griffin-Lim (M08) and no listener rated it, as listeners already did for ECoG synthesis in 2019 [@anumanchipalli2019speech]. Its advantage over direct spectrogram or GAN decoding rests on three participants (Supplementary Fig. 10). The causal PCC of 0.797 is within-participant reconstruction of 50 trained words (M12).
